target.title: fix(codex): warn when routes use stale embedded binaries
target.body:
Related: #99951

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators could see OpenClaw's Codex plugin and the host `codex` CLI as current while `/codex` provider routes still ran an older embedded Codex binary from the active `@openclaw/codex` package.

Fleet evidence in #99951 showed `@openclaw/codex@2026.6.11` embedding `@openai/codex@0.139.0` on multiple users while the host CLI was newer. `openclaw plugins update codex --dry-run` still reported the plugin as current, so the stale route binary was invisible to the normal update/health path.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change makes the Codex route binary contract explicit in three places:

- bumps the managed Codex route runtime from `@openai/codex@0.142.4` to the current patch `0.142.5`, including shrinkwrap and lockfile platform aliases;
- extends official plugin drift detection with `runtimeDependencyDrifts`, so an active `@openclaw/codex` install can warn even when the plugin package version matches the gateway;
- adds a publish/pretag package guard for `@openclaw/codex` so `package.json`, `npm-shrinkwrap.json`, and platform aliases must agree before release.

The drift guard checks exact-pinned official installs too. Exact pins may opt out of gateway-version lockstep, but they should not opt out of an approved route-runtime dependency contract.

Codex CLI source inspection before the change confirmed why this must key off the plugin package tree, not `/usr/bin/codex`: `codex-cli/bin/codex.js` resolves the platform package from the installed `@openai/codex` package (`require.resolve(.../package.json)`) and spawns that binary; the Codex package builder publishes those platform packages as aliases under `@openai/codex-*`.

## User Impact

Operators now get an actionable `gateway status --deep` / doctor warning when an active Codex route plugin embeds a stale or missing `@openai/codex` runtime. Release maintainers also get a package-level guard that blocks source-vs-shrinkwrap drift before another stale Codex route package can be published.

This PR proves detection and release blocking logic. It does not mutate or remediate any customer VM, and it does not claim all fleets are fixed.

## Evidence

Fleet evidence packet, read-only: `/Volumes/LEXAR/Codex/codex-openclaw-route-version-checks/2026-07-04-david-poku-golden.md`

Focused local validation:

```text
pnpm install --lockfile-only --ignore-scripts
node scripts/generate-npm-shrinkwrap.mjs --package-dir extensions/codex --check
pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/codex/package.json extensions/codex/npm-shrinkwrap.json extensions/codex/src/app-server/version.ts scripts/lib/plugin-npm-release.ts src/cli/daemon-cli/status.print.test.ts src/cli/daemon-cli/status.print.ts src/commands/doctor-workspace-status.test.ts src/commands/doctor-workspace-status.ts src/plugins/plugin-version-drift.test.ts src/plugins/plugin-version-drift.ts test/plugin-npm-release.test.ts pnpm-lock.yaml
git diff --check
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/plugin-version-drift.test.ts src/cli/daemon-cli/status.print.test.ts src/commands/doctor-workspace-status.test.ts extensions/codex/src/manifest.test.ts test/plugin-npm-release.test.ts
pnpm tsgo:test:src
```

Focused Vitest result: 5 shards passed, 99 tests passed.
